CHROMIUM: config: enable CONFIG_SECURITY_PERF_EVENTS_RESTRICT This CL enables CONFIG_SECURITY_PERF_EVENTS_RESTRICT in the base config for Chrome OS. CONFIG_SECURITY_PERF_EVENTS_RESTRICT was introduced in CL:420490 ("ANDROID: FROMLIST: security,perf: Allow further restriction of perf_event_open"). When CONFIG_SECURITY_PERF_EVENTS_RESTRICT is set, the default value of sysctl.perf_event_paranoid is set to 3, which causes the perf_event_open syscall to disallow any access to performance events by users without the CAP_SYS_ADMIN capability. g: remove superfluous DCRYPTO_SHA256_init in HMAC implementation DCRYPTO_HMAC_SHA256_init makes two calls to DCRYPTO_SHA256_init() without an intervening HASH_final() call. This is incorrect usage of the the hashing API, and results in the hardware SHA engine getting locked for the life-time of the process (and resulting in all future hash calls falling back to the software implementation). This bug manifested itself when introducing NVRAM encryption, which requires the hardware SHA engine to be available for key generation. BRANCH=none BUG=chrome-os-partner:55331 TEST=TCG tests pass Change-Id: Ia4ccb6a6d64636c4618ef775291442975f3f1f92 Signed-off-by: nagendra modadugu <ngm@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/430154 Commit-Ready: Nagendra Modadugu <ngm@google.com> Tested-by: Nagendra Modadugu <ngm@google.com> Reviewed-by: Marius Schilder <mschilder@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Vadim Bendebury <vbendeb@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: ath10k: don't create monitor interface for OTHER_BSS filter ath10k had a workaround which created an internal monitor interface to support the OTHER_BSS filter. ath10k firmware sets RX filters on behalf of the interface type, which now includes OTHER_BSS frames for mesh. However, an RX filter flag to accept all multicast and broadcast frames is still needed. Creating the monitor interface seems to cause a problem with continuous BF requests in a mesh of more than 2 nodes. This patch, combined with a firmware to fix the missing RX filter flags avoids this issue. NOTE: for upstreaming we still need to handle backward compatibility through feature flags or such. For example this driver combined with old firmware which doesn't set the multicast RX filter breaks broadcast traffic (ARP) in mesh. BUG=chrome-os-partner: 60014 TEST=3 node mesh reboot one of the nodes during ping, don't see traffic interruption while NDP loop is happening. Change-Id: If3c5cebff213469669efa1889326121641074409 Signed-off-by: Thomas Pedersen <twp@codeaurora.org> Signed-off-by: Tamizh chelvam <c_traja@qti.qualcomm.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/411750 Commit-Ready: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org> Tested-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org>

g: add means of building node locked images When debug enabled cr50 image is signed, the default manifest passed to the signer is util/signer/ec_RW-manifest-dev.json. Images signed with this manifest will not run on devices where the RO part is fused for production. It is possible to build node locked images for such devices, but the manifest must include the lines "DEV_ID0": <value>. "DEV_ID1": <value>, with the values matching the chip the image is built for. This patch allows to pass the values in the make command line or the environment, defined as follows: H1_DEVIDS='<num 1> <num 2>' When this value is defined, the default manifest is edited to add the required lines. One side effect of this patch is that the temp file where the edited manifest is placed to is not deleted. BRANCH=none BUG=none TEST=verified that images still can be built for both dev RW and prod RO (node locked) with both debug features enabled and disabled (CR50_DEV set and not set) Change-Id: I0e81fc9aa65aa4d239e60de6047e2470f6eeaf50 Signed-off-by: Vadim Bendebury <vbendeb@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/428337 Reviewed-by: Randall Spangler <rspangler@chromium.org>

login: set less restrictive value for perf_event_paranoid under dev-mode /proc/sys/kernel/perf_event_paranoid controls the use of kernel perf events system by users without the CAP_SYS_ADMIN capability. On systems with Chrome OS kernel 3.14 or later, we now enable CONFIG_SECURITY_PERF_EVENTS_RESTRICT in kernel, which sets the default value of perf_event_paranoid to a more restrictive level "3", instead of the previous default value "1". We already allow dev-mode only syscalls, such as perf_event_open(), to be exposed to the Android container when the system is in developer mode (CL:425454). This CL restores perf_event_paranoid to the less restrictive level "1" when the system is in developer mode in order to allow the following mapping: Chrome OS | Android | Kernel ---------------+------------------------+----------------------- verified mode | security.perf_harden=1 | perf_event_paranoid=3 ---------------+------------------------+----------------------- developer mode | security.perf_harden=0 | perf_event_paranoid=1 BUG=b:33450588 TEST=Tested the following: - On samus-cheets (kernel 3.14): * Under developer mode, sign in a registered user, verify that /proc/sys/kernel/perf_event_paranoid is set to 1 by default. * Under verified mode, sign in a registered user, verify that /proc/sys/kernel/perf_event_paranoid is set to 3 by default. - On a system with kernel 3.8, verify that /proc/sys/kernel/perf_event_paranoid is set to 1 by default in absence of the CONFIG_SECURITY_PERF_EVENTS_RESTRICT kernel option.
